messages:
jamie (support): FYI ACME prod is seeing 502/503 to their private service endpoint svc.api.acme.internal after the subnet migration at ~08:30 UTC. Some requests also show TLS cert mismatch. Customer reports intermittent 503.

alex (SE): Do we have a quick repro curl + dig output? Might be resolving to public LB after the migration.

jamie (support): Pasted what customer ran: 
```
$ dig +short svc.api.acme.internal
52.14.23.88
10.3.45.12
```
They say it should only return private ENI IPs (10.3.45.12). First IP is public LB.

ingrid (infra): That smells like split-horizon / duplicate private hosted zone. Check Route53 for same zone name in other accounts or a private zone associated to shared services VPC.

jamie (support): I checked quickly in our org view — there's a private hosted zone with the same name in the mgmt account that was accidentally associated to the shared-services VPC yesterday during infra cleanup.

dns-bot: automated check: found 2 private hosted zones for zone name "api.acme.internal" across accounts (account-12345, account-98765). account-98765 zone is associated to prod VPC: vpc-0a1b2c3d.

sre-oncall: If the mgmt-account zone is associated to the VPC, Route53 can return records from that hosted zone even if a different account owns the intended zone. That would explain public LB entry. Also check node-local DNS cache on nodes for stale answers.

alex (SE): Steps to validate from our side: 
- From a pod: `nslookup svc.api.acme.internal` and `dig @127.0.0.53 svc.api.acme.internal`
- `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id ZONEID` for both zones to confirm associations
- `curl -v --resolve svc.api.acme.internal:443:10.3.45.12 https://svc.api.acme.internal/health` to bypass DNS if needed.

jamie (support): Ran the pod test for customer: 
```
$ kubectl exec -it svc-abc -- dig +short svc.api.acme.internal
52.14.23.88
10.3.45.12
```
Pod DNS is returning public LB first. Customer hit TLS mismatch because the public LB cert is for `api.acme.com` and pod expects `svc.api.acme.internal`.

dev-hugo: If it's cross-account, easiest fix is to disassociate mgmt-account's private hosted zone from the prod VPC (if that's safe). Otherwise change association in prod to point only to the intended zone.

ingrid (infra): I flagged with infra owner in mgmt account, they confirmed the zone was associated by mistake during a move of shared-services VPC. They removed the association at 09:12 UTC.

jamie (support): After disassociation we asked the customer to flush node-local caches and restart a couple of pods. Commands we gave them: 
```
# on each node
sudo systemctl restart node-local-dns
# or for k8s node-local-dns DaemonSet
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/node-local-dns
# restart affected pods
kubectl delete pod -l app=svc-api -n acme-prod
```

rachel (customer): Confirming — after those steps we see only private IPs now and errors stopped. Thanks! :tada:

jamie (support): Customer reports successful test: `dig` now returns only `10.3.45.12` and their app no longer sees TLS mismatch.

alex (SE): Root cause summary: duplicate private hosted zone in mgmt account was associated to the prod VPC, causing split-horizon to return unintended public LB record. That plus node-local DNS cache meant pods kept the wrong answer until restart.

ingrid (infra): Remediation applied: disassociated mgmt-account zone from prod VPC. Confirmed no other VPCs incorrectly associated. Also asked mgmt infra to add a guardrail to prevent accidental cross-account private zone associations for prod VPCs.

jamie (support): Action items: 
- (ingrid) Add automation rule to detect duplicate private zones with same name across accounts and alert (P0 for infra).
- (alex) Add a one-liner runbook we can paste to customers for flush/restart steps.
- (jamie) Send customer postmortem + communication.

dev-hugo: Also we should add a pre-migration check: "no private hosted zones with same name exist in other accounts associated to target VPC".

sre-oncall: Marking for postmortem; assign owner: ingrid.

jamie (support): Customer confirmed full recovery at 09:40 UTC. Closing ticket once PM emailed.

rachel (customer): Appreciate the quick turnaround everyone!
_meta: generated for dataset: support thread about private DNS resolution failures, split-horizon and cross-account Route53 hosted zone association
